text:
maria: Heads up — nightly eval for redwood-3b-quant shows a nondeterministic quality spike on promptset 'billing-flows'. Failures jump around between runs, not constant. Saw a cluster between ~03:10-03:21 UTC. Filing here for triage. :thinking_face:

eval-bot: nightly-run 1769004300 summary: model=redwood-3b-quant, promptsets=12, failing_cases=28, top-failure-promptset=billing-flows (28 failures). CI artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/1769004300

raj: Do we have any infra changes last night? caching/batching flags?

lena: We flipped two runtime flags in canary at 02:45 UTC: async_prefetch=true and prefix_cache_ttl_swap=true. Both landed in inference/runtime v3.2.1.

sam: Can you paste minimal repro? I'll try to run locally.

maria: Minimal repro I used (still non-determ):
```
python -m rdw_eval.run --model redwood-3b-quant --promptset billing-flows --seed 42 --batch-size 8 --runs 5
```
On my laptop two runs with same args produced different top-k completions after token 22 depending on alignment.

andre: My suspicion: async prefetch + narrow batching is causing KV slot reuse between adjacent requests when prefetch insertion races with slot assignment. I've seen similar with shared prefix cache aliasing.

infra-bot: deploy log: inference/runtime@v3.2.1 -> flags: async_prefetch=true (default), prefix_cache_mode=shared, batch_coalescing=v2. Deployed to canary / us-west-2 at 02:45 UTC.

raj: Here's a dump from one of the failing runs (sanitized):
```
[03:12:10.123] REQ id=aaa prefix_hash=0x7f1a slot=57 KV_LOOKUP hit=true
[03:12:10.125] REQ id=bbb prefix_hash=0x3c2d slot=57 KV_INSERT from_prefetch=true
[03:12:10.126] REQ id=aaa generate token=22 ... output=<X>
[03:12:10.127] REQ id=bbb generate token=22 ... output=<Y>
```
Two different requests ended up with the same slot index 57 within a tight window. That smells like prefetched KV wrote into a slot a different request later read.

lena: Ugh. We intentionally set prefix_cache_mode=shared to improve hit rate across tenants in dedicated tests, but this means slot assignment must be deterministic per-request namespace. If there's any race, outputs will diverge.

maria: Quick config test: I ran the nightly harness with REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE_MODE=isolated for the job. Results: failures dropped from 28 -> 2 out of 200. With shared + prefetch=true it's back to ~27. So config mitigates.

sam: That strongly implicates cache isolation. Could be bug in slot salting or in the async prefetch path where the prefetched item uses a global slot allocator.

andre: Root cause hypothesis: async prefetch enqueues KV material for write but doesn't bind it to request-scoped namespace before insertion. When coalesced batches flush, insertion can race with other request lookups that use the same slot index computed from a narrower transient hash. Proposed fix: append per-request namespace salt before final slot index calc, and ensure prefetch insert uses same salted namespace. Also add a small atomic compare-and-swap on slot ownership at insert time.

raj: I'll add a unit/regression test in the runtime harness: spawn two concurrent requests with contrived prefixes that map to same slot with and without prefetch on, and assert deterministic outputs across repeated runs. Test name: test_prefix_cache_prefetch_isolation.

lena: For immediate mitigation I'll roll a canary revert for async_prefetch on canary clusters and set nightly to isolated mode until we ship a fix. Will open a rollout PR.

maria: Created ticket INFR-1234: "prefix cache prefetch race -> nondeterministic eval failures" and linked logs + repro. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-1234 Assigned to @raj and @andre.

sam: Also adding a nightly evaluation variant that toggles batch alignment seeds (aligned vs misaligned) to catch this class of bugs. Seeds + batch boundary fuzzing found this quickly.

andre: I'll prototype the namespace-salt + CAS slot ownership patch and post a draft patch by EOD. If small, we can ship a patch to canary tomorrow.

maria: Thanks all. For tracking: short action list in ticket: 1) revert async_prefetch on canary (lena), 2) add regression test (raj), 3) implement atomic insert + per-request salt (andre), 4) expand nightly batch alignment fuzzing (sam).

raj: one more note: add an alert if nightly shows >5x variance in failure counts across 3 consecutive runs — that helped flag this. :eyes:

lena: noted. I'll file a small ops alert.

maria: ok closing triage here, will update ticket when we have a canary rollback and test in place. :white_check_mark:
